text: Third is recruitment, which I have explained before.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think although it is very competitive, Singapore continues to be an attractive location for foreign nurses to want to come to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The healthcare profession continues to be quite attractive to our locals as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, one in 25 students will join nursing and I cannot hope for more.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is not bad at all considering the number of options they have.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I think we are getting our fair share of local talent and we are competitive in hiring foreign nurses as well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But of course, I hope the House, having raised all these issues, will support the necessary steps that we need to take in order to recruit local as well as foreign nurses.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our Public Service has a long history of inter-agency collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It was a period when we witnessed the tremendous potential of inter-agency cooperation, united in a common objective to overcome a national crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you look at our schools, they kept education going, shifted to home-based learning only for a couple of months.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our economic and social agencies worked together to support businesses and workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Various agencies got together to set up quarantine facilities, testing and community care facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I cannot emphasise enough how much that meant to the hospital system, which would have, otherwise, borne the full brunt of the pandemic and we would have likely collapsed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Recently, a well-known Chinese infectious disease expert, Dr Zhang Wen Hong, after he observed how life in China has gone back to normal during the May Day Golden Week, he wrote a blog post and he said, “It was as if nothing had happened, yet everything has happened”.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It was a rather poignant expression of the post-crisis state of mind which may be relevant in Singapore and relevant to today’s debate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We do not want to hang on to and relive the crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to walk out of the shadows, put it behind us and look into the future.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The experience and lessons learnt will reshape the way we look at healthcare and the way we look at inter-agency collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Those cannot be forgotten and go to waste.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I share Members’ hope that while the crisis may be over and peace time workload has resumed, it cannot be business as usual.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should usher in a new era of even tighter inter-agency collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And this is especially relevant for healthcare for two reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Number one, as I have explained, ageing is probably the biggest social transformation for Singapore in the next 10 years, as we become a “super-aged” society.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will have implications across multiple policy areas – in employment, in our competitiveness, retirement adequacy, urban planning, education and, of course, healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will draw Ministries together to work in concert.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have explained in this House why and what we are doing in this transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In other words, health is not just relevant to patients who have fallen sick.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And that is why we now regard the healthcare system as three inter-linked systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Janet Ang has just explained this earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, we have the acute care system, which is essential in ensuring that those who are sick get treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third system is the aged care system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The default for aged care cannot be nursing homes or seniors living alone with no social support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In other countries, loneliness and social isolation of seniors have become an epidemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think it is one of the reasons why length of stay has gone up, especially after COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we can do this right, I think we can do what Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested – integrate care across medical and social realms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And we need to urgently step up this whole-of-society efforts to enable our seniors to live their golden years in dignity, age actively in their community with their friends and family, involve them in activities including training programmes, like what Mr Mark Chay has suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To make Health for All possible, we need the contribution of every stakeholder, public or private.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When healthcare is mostly treating sickness, it falls under the domain of hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But when healthcare is about creating health and caring for people in their homes and communities, it becomes everyone’s business.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, in order to realise Health for All, we also need All for Health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think this is really the spirit behind the Motion put forward by the Members.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In particular, the following stakeholders can make significant contributions to health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many of us spend a considerable amount of our adult lives at work and hence the workplace is highly influential in shaping our health habits.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I value our existing partnerships with NTUC, SNEF and the Tripartite Oversight Committee on Workplace Safety and Health (TOC) who have been working with companies to promote good workplace health practices.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With Healthier SG, employers can work closely with your panel doctors to join Healthier SG and to continue providing regular and proper screenings for employees, provide healthier canteen food, physical activity programmes, mental well-being programmes and better work-life balance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We also urge employers to play their part in making sure those eligible are all part of Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By promoting good health, employers will have more productive and happier employees, which is good for businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua has shared about MCCY’s efforts to mobilise the community to foster social cohesion, promote health and develop a strong partnership with family doctors.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam also suggested the need to have activities that cater to different segments of population and their varied interests.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We welcome other ground-up initiatives and activities that rally the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we take a walk in our public parks today, we can spot many of these activities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many of them not organised by any agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Friends getting together to cycle, run, play football.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All of them are now part of the healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, good health starts from our values, habits and choices.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our schools help to build this foundation of health literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They introduce our young to sports, help them make friends and form social groups, teach them life skills and knowledge to be useful citizens, all of which are essential building blocks to good health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As mentioned by Minister of State Gan Siow Huang earlier, through the years, MOE has worked with MOH to thoughtfully infuse health education in its curriculum from early childhood to primary, secondary and tertiary education.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Maybe that is the right button to push, I do not know.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, MOH, MOE and MSF; we are studying the linkages between early education and health, and developing possible interventions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Information and media literacy is our first line of defense against false and viral health myths.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to work with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and other media agencies to do this, just as we did during COVID-19 to dispel falsehoods about vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Healthier SG gives us an opportunity to address the problem of health misinformation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is because we are advocating and trying to build stronger patient-doctor relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because with a trusted relationship and the family doctor and his care team knowing the health condition and history of the patient, they become the patient’s trusted source of medical information and advice.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In this digital era of information overload, online falsehoods, myths and AI bots, perhaps what we need in healthcare is stronger human relationships, especially between doctors and patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We can use technology to strengthen the relationship and improve the quality of care rather than replace the human relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That must ultimately be the mode of co-existence between humans and AI.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These are many examples of how agencies are coming together to better support health and we are committed to continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am mindful that our Nominated Members of Parliament are coming to the end of their term.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I do not know for sure, but Leader told me, it might be your second last Sitting.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I know some of you hope to have the assurance that even as you step down, the issues close to your heart continue to receive attention in this Chamber.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, I feel honoured and privileged – although it got me a bit busy – that you have chosen to table a Motion on healthcare, just as you have actively been speaking up on healthcare issues during your term.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In particular, Dr Tan Yia Swam, who was also the President of the Singapore Medical Association (SMA).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: She has been a strong advocate for various healthcare-related issues.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I attended an SMA dinner some time ago hosted by her.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In her speech during that event – it is public, so I think I can say it – she said that she was an angry young doctor.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And now, you are a less angry middle-aged doctor.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the difference is that you have learned how to channel your energy to a greater good and be a better advocate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I say Dr Tan is doing a good job, both in SMA as well as in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But I do not think Dr Tan is angry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is important that we are passionate in our cause and be active in our advocacy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I greatly appreciate this Motion, highlighting the need for MOH to work with other agencies and for other agencies to support us.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, we have MOE and MCCY's political officeholders (POHs) deliver their speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Actually, we could have gotten many more, but we did not want to prolong the debate for too long.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ageing is going to be the big challenge that affects all of us – and MOH cannot be alone in this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The passion and activism of our NMPs help uplift the standard of debate in this House and bode well for the democratic discourse for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, please rest assured that the issues close to your hearts will continue to be given due attention in this House, even as your term comes to an end.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will be a new batch of NMPs who are passionate about issues too, and take up the issues that you care about.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For NMPs, after you have stepped down, I hope you will continue to advise and cheer us on, at the side.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, let us all continue to advocate for a better healthcare system for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Health is for All and All is for health.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Okay, maybe not so angry anymore, after all your kind words.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If you are going to stay 10 years like Mr Gan, then I will continue to advise and help for 10 years.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: First of all, I thank all my fellow NMPs in attendance who have each shared their insights into how healthcare can be supported in their various sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: This is the kind of fresh ideas that we need to have a synergistic whole.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I thank all Members for their various speeches covering a wide range of topics in relation to support for healthcare, namely: (a) recruit, reskill and retain healthcare workers; (b) fair pay, reasonable working hours; (c) financing and business needs; (d) better IT systems; (e) taking a firm stand against bullying and harassment; (f) emphasis on prevention and primary care; (g) legal protection and support; and (h) looking after vulnerable groups, in particular, children, the elderly, migrant workers and the differently-abled.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: However, I must address some of the points that the Member Mr Leong brought up yesterday.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate his points about reviewing MediSave but I urge him to have in-depth discussions with MOH to better understand the current funding and to help in future reviews if necessary.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If any of you know residents in financial distress, please direct them to an experienced medical social worker who will be able to further advise on additional available subsidies.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I also need to seek clarification from Mr Leong on his comment that, I quote, "drug prices should not be marked up unreasonably for non-subsidised patients to cross-subsidise subsidised patients." Firstly, is there have evidence of this happening?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If I can use another food analogy other than chicken rice, a can of soda can be sixty cents at a budget grocery mart, $1.30 at a super mart, $1.60 at a coffee shop, $3 in a restaurant and $5 in a hotel.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: How much is a reasonable mark-up for medications?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Would Mr Leong also want taxpayers to pay for everyone?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I also thank the political office holders from different Ministries for your assurance and commitment to support healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Minister of State Gan Siow Huang has also given an overview of how teaching on exercise and healthy eating is integrated at all levels of education.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The professional bodies will continue to work closely with MOH in resolving issues within healthcare, especially those that pertain to training and working hours.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Honestly, only clinicians truly understand the delicate balance needed.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am glad that we are all aligned in this – that healthcare has to be a whole-of-Government effort.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In my closing, I come full circle, back to "Why".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Why do we stand up to advocate for a cause?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: To leave behind a better world than the one we were born in.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Recent news regarding the next round of NMP applications has again raised some criticism.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I believe the NMP role has given an ordinary citizen like myself the chance to voice opinions at a national platform.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Ordinary, because I am a struggling working mother in the sandwiched generation.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Ordinary, because I also fear and worry about my children's future.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: What kind of Singapore will my children grow up in?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Fellow MPs will appreciate how hard it is to prepare for a speech.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It is not just simply coming up to the microphone and saying some fancy words.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is background research, sticking to the timing before getting scolded by the Speaker or Deputy Speakers; and speaking the truth – in a palatable way and driving home a point.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I commented before – we are all talking a lot, but who is listening?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The livestreaming only has 400 plus viewers, usually.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: A few people will deliberately make funny clips of our mistakes or slip-ups.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Once I get over the embarrassment of my own, I have to say, it is actually very funny, so, thanks for making us laugh!

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But the people I am really speaking to are fellow citizens who share my interest in the larger good of Singapore, the citizens listening in and considering policy.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Civil servants are individuals who would have their own different political beliefs and alignments.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Blindly supporting or opposing any political party or mocking NMPs for being mouthpieces or puppets or blaming the Government for everything – I ask you, is it logical?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Before reacting and speaking, consider three points: one, is it true?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If the answer is no to any of the above, maybe it is better not to say.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure that many of you have friends who are in healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Do speak to them and understand the problems we face.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Create your own small little informal think tanks and brainstorm on how to solve larger healthcare issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: For all the people listening in, whether you are working in Ministries, whether you are an ordinary citizen like myself, I hope that you will also think of ways to ensure that healthcare gets the support it needs and prioritise your own healthcare needs.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We now live in a rapidly changing and volatile world.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Look at how COVID-19 brought the world to a standstill for three lost years.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Look at the Ukraine war, the US bank collapses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: History repeats itself – maybe in a much faster cycle than before.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The modern person has to be able to adapt to a world where answers may be less obvious, where there is no rulebook or 10-year-series to refer to.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There may be no single right answer and choices will have trade-offs.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But are we building up on useful knowledge or frittering our time away on social media in mindless entertainment?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I see patients and the medical treatment algorithms are actually quite simple.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But frequently, emotional stress gets in the way.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: This manifests as hesitation, fear, worry and even anger at me – "Why is there a lump?" I understand but it is not easy to process the onslaught of negative emotions.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare workers, teachers, drivers – all frontline service workers, in fact – have received the brunt of a lot of negative outpouring of emotions.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: People being unhappy in their daily lives without even realising it, feeling irritable, snappy, overly critical, worried about everything and feeling unable to cope.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I repeat a point from my previous speech.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If you suffer from anxiety or anger management, do not take it out on your healthcare worker.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Even though I am a breast surgeon, I cannot just operate on the cancer.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have to consider the patient in her whole entirety.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Her overall health – does she have other medical conditions that impact her surgery and recovery?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Her preferred language – does she fully understand what I am saying?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Is she going to be well supported at home and at the workplace or will she forgo care because she perceives that others' needs come before her?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: First, walk the ground, get real feedback and acknowledge problems in healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Second, continue education at all levels of engagement.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Let us learn from the mistakes of the past so that we do not repeat it.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It has been an eventful and fun NMP journey.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: To all MPs from both sides of the House, I am glad for the chance to get to know you all as people and real humans, not just as public figures on your posters.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: This is my last speech in this Chamber.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The next time we meet again, it may be when I complain to you at Meet-the-People sessions.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If I may, I will pray for wisdom and kindness for you as you all continue to debate meaningfully on issues to guide Singapore safely through future challenges.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am about to put the question to the House.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: You have a clarification arising from a speech that has been given?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Do you have a clarification for Dr Tan?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Yes, you want to respond to her questions, right?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: According to my understanding and a lot of the feedback from residents, they pay different prices when they are in different classes.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But from a certain angle, which I have mentioned in my speech, it is okay to charge the services, but why is there such a big difference in the drug prices being charged for different classes?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do not know why Dr Tan raised it as an issue.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Maybe I can also clarify with Dr Tan whether she agrees with our proposal that the Government should actually start a central procurement process for all drugs in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Yes, I would like to respond because I am a doctor and I think I know a bit about healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: I think firstly, regarding bills, to the hon Member, it would be useful to ask your affected residents to approach the hospital's business office that they were in to seek clarification on the bill breakdown.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: There are very clear explanations and breakdowns on the tiers of subsidies available and different drugs, whether it is branded or generic, have very, very clear costings.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: So, I would like to know more details of the case rather than make a blanket statement that the costings are unfair.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: In the private sector, though, may I respectfully state that all doctors in the private sector have our own business models and different ways of generating income.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: So, not all doctors may want to be part of the Government effort.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: We can take it back to the professional bodies and further get our members' feedback.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung, you have a clarification?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I just thought that it is not very fair that the NMP has to answer a policy question.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is better for MOH to say something.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are deliberately catered to a variegated market.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, when we put forward an idea – but, luckily, it is from the Member and not from me.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we put forward an idea to say, "Let us all sell at the same price", actually, doctors, their rice bowls gets affected and it can be quite a major issue for them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think there is some wisdom in what Dr Tan Yia Swam said.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think that is how we reign in unnecessary healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But really, I think this is a Motion about Ministries and all of us, all stakeholders coming together, a very meaningful Motion.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I would urge that we do not prolong further this to-ing and fro-ing and let us give our stepping-down NMPs strong support for their very meaningful Motion.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I declare my interest as a breast surgeon in private practice and my various medical leadership roles as an appointed member of the Singapore Medical Council and the Vice President of the Singapore Medical Association.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, I speak as a daughter to elderly parents and parents-in-law and as a mother to children with medical conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   As the saying goes "Doctors have the heart of a parent".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Doctors should be caring and concerned towards their patients, just like parents to their children.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Doctors should have this mentality throughout their life.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: However, patients are not necessarily willing to be treated like a child all their lives.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: When a child is young, he is ignorant and will obey the instructions of his parents.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As he grows up, he will start to rebel against the instructions of his parents.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Thirty years ago, patients would generally listen to the doctor's words.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But now, due to advanced technology and easy access to information, more and more patients will question doctors' diagnoses or instructions, or even challenge them.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): Why does anyone stand up to advocate for certain causes?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We want to leave behind a better world than what we were born in.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As a patient, I want my doctor to look after my best interests and not be worried about being complained or sued unfairly.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As a doctor, I want to focus on my patient's medical conditions, her needs and wants.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: So many other factors influence this relationship – different kinds of health-seeking behaviours, different health beliefs, financing models, expectations of outcomes, customer service, social media marketing, business entities seeking to profit in the healthcare sector.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Why am I pushing for a whole-of-Government effort?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare spending is the second highest in the national budget.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The emphasis on building more hospitals, polyclinics, Healthier SG and recruiting staff – this cannot go on indefinitely.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: These are some well-known facts in our medical community.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Health news magazines frequently report these, but people do not care until it happens to them.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Most people have a healthcare encounter only when they are sick and that is too late.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: That is why the institution has to remember and pass on the teaching.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It feels like the whole country, even the whole world, has moved on after COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But if you look back at the history of pandemics, the next one will be here – maybe in 10 years, maybe in five.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We need to be ready for the next pandemic, for the silver tsunami, for the mental health crisis.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I urge for all of you to adopt a mindset change.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I urge every Ministry, every Government official, every public servant – in fact, anyone listening right now – to think in terms of how to better teach our people to look after their health and prevent illness.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Next, support for healthcare workers – what does it mean?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It cannot be just a one-time snapshot, a once-off wellness event, a "thank you" campaign, a medal.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But beyond that, support for healthcare workers should be a deeply rooted respect and acknowledgement of the nature of our work.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Many of us see our work as a calling.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Much like those in our armed forces who protect our nation, healthcare workers protect the health and well-being of our people.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It is not just business transactions selling remedies.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: What kind of support do healthcare workers want then?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Back to my analogy about the parent-child relationship.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I hope the doctor-patient relationship will be mutually loving and respectful.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot be just using that one day of Father's or Mother's Day to love our parents, right?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Take into account what we say, listen and involve us in decision-making.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: More than a decade ago, as a junior doctor, I remember there was one day when there was a mini commotion in the operating theatre.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We were told to recall our chits so that the queue of patients waiting for surgery is cleared up.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I demanded to know why and I was told, "Minister is visiting." I remember being indignant and told the sister-in-charge, "Let him see.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Let him see how swamped we are." Of course, I was chased away while the welcoming party walked him around.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I was an angry young doctor, but I resolved to learn to be a better advocate for change.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Leaders need to walk the ground and healthcare workers need to learn to speak up better for ourselves.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Maybe it is not in our nature to ever admit defeat or ask for help, because it implies weakness and we are determined to stay strong for our patients.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Maybe that is why so many of us work until breaking point.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In the past two years, mainstream news and social media gave much attention to bed shortages, long working hours of junior doctors and nurses, bullying and harassment, but I tell you this is nothing new to us.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Corridor beds, lodgers in tentage, conversion of day surgery beds to acute care beds.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There were patients fit for discharge but the common social request was to keep the patient until the weekend because the children cannot take leave to bring him home or the need to wait until the helper arrives in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: So, instead of operating, I was there doing bed management and being scolded by family members for being heartless.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Then, when I go down to finally attend to the new patients waiting, I get scolded for making them wait very long.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We did six to eight calls a month.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Doctors, nurses, lab technicians, couriers, healthcare attendants – everyone in the healthcare system is trying our best to meet demands; and sometimes, we cannot deliver.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: How many of us have just gone to cry and hide in the toilet for a while?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We have seen the ups and downs of problems in the past decades.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The removal of the guideline of fees, coupled with as-charged plans, leading to escalating costs, due to multiple factors that we are still trying to address now in the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (MHIC).

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Changes to residency training, leading to the loss of mentorship, loss of a sense of belonging by the trainees.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Shorter training periods with consequences in some specialties.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The privatisation and commercialisation of healthcare is a "necessary evil".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Someone has to ensure there is money to run a sustainable business.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But when healthcare workers are treated as a commodity by administrators, it is yet another bad influence on the doctor-patient relationship.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In the private sector, business costs are increasing due to rental, manpower costs and pressure from business entities; perpetual problems with poor IT systems; a brain drain of experienced nurses, allied health and even doctors.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have previously spoken on wellness and alternative health services, which are not regulated and which sometimes do more harm than good.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Poor use of Google leading to badly written search engine optimisation articles that further increases the disconnect between doctors and patients.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some family physicians have expressed their perceived difficulties to onboard Healthier SG.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am saying doctors are worried about these changes.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We have lived through changes with adverse outcomes and we feel really helpless when others dictate how we should practise medicine.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We should learn from the mistakes of the past so that we do not repeat it, but humans have short memories and few people have the time or commitment to dig into history.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Political office bearers come and go, but for most doctors and nurses, we are here for a lifetime.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The longest serving Minister for Health is Mr Gan Kim Yong for 10 years and for that, I thank him for the warm and supportive relationship he had with our profession, which Mr Ong Ye Kung has kindly continued – hopefully, for the future, after my speech.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is no one who is giving the healthcare system his full attention and thought.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Many feel unease and unhappiness at "the system", but there is no one whose job is to really evaluate and improve the system.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, experts from other service industries are imported to provide opinions, get paid consultancy fees – and they leave, while we care so hard and so badly, that it hurts.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Even with all my lobbying for the private sector, for reviews into Shield plans, corporate insurance, concierge services, third-party administrators (TPAs), many have heard but might not be listening.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Sadly, even my own doctors do not pay close attention to my advocacy efforts and keep repeating the same old grouses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some are aware but do not dare to take action.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: They might be afraid of losing their livelihoods if they do not play by the rules of TPAs who have come between doctors and patients.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have frequently said to my peers that it is common sense that a business should be profitable, but we should never profiteer here from people's suffering.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare providers are in a no-win situation – getting complaints for long waiting times in Government hospitals, getting accused of overcharging in private.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We all want perfection – cheap, fast and good.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have repeatedly vouched for our restructured hospitals.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We have all trained and worked there at some point and they provide good quality care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Sometimes, the communications may not be as clear or personable, simply because it is a very large team-based practice.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I think restructured hospitals are cheap and good, and it is hard to be fast.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We all learn through mentorship, by examining small lumps, do our first operations.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is consultant lead practice and there is a specialist in charge of your medical journey.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: When you meet a young doctor with a heart, I hope you help the doctor to train and grow.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some of you will choose to go private if you can afford it because you get personal service, it is generally faster, there is more privacy because it is a much smaller team attending to you.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But then I ask for your understanding that every doctor runs a business and there are various models that are used with various business costs.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If you find a doctor that you trust and there is clear communication and transparency, I hope you will also give him the support he needs.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have listed a string of perennial problems, which are complex and systemic, and that I do not expect any one person to solve.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Stay with me as I share my views on education and cross-collaboration.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I think the commonest method is by frequent exposure and repetition.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Three times a day, maybe five times or even more.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: So, if I ask about chicken rice, there will be a very hot-blooded robust debate on which store is the best, comparing roast chicken versus steamed chicken, the ginger, the chilli.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Enthusiasts will even know the exact cost breakdown from different stores: how much you charge for extra chilli, extra rice, an upgrade to thigh meat.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But how many of us need major surgery or admission for a major illness?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There are some patients with complex medical issues who have been in and out of hospitals.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The healthcare team ends up knowing the patients and families very well over time.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Such families will likely also be very aware of how treatment costs are like.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: For most people though, the first major illness is the first time ever that we have to seek medical care in the hospital.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: That is not a good time to find out how expensive healthcare is.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: One is already worried about their cancer diagnosis and the impact on survival, side effects and potential complications of treatment, responsibilities of work versus family.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I know I was when I had to handle the bills for an open heart surgery.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The problem is most healthy people do not bother to check these until they encounter health issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If it is an elective surgery, there is time for financial counselling, pre-authorisation and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But in an emergency, the team would deliver the necessary life-threatening treatments first.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The patient and their family may be saddled with a big debt.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Or the hospital writes off bad debt – not often, I believe, but I know that this happens when we have a foreign worker with no health insurance, just an accident policy and there is no or inadequate cover.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Same for locals who are not familiar with the product they bought, whether it is a plan for hospitalisation, critical illness or early cancer plan.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Maybe they did not know about exclusion terms or coverage limits.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I picked up this lingo and knowledge only in these recent three years and I hate that I have to know it.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: People need to learn how to navigate our healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some years ago, I started a blog specifically on how to enter the healthcare system, the different paths available and the pros and cons of each.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Since then, I have seen several well-written articles.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is no need to keep re-inventing the wheel.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Collect these, have a good library of such articles in the central repository and let it be the main reference for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: People do not actively care until it happens to them.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Look at global warming, does the average person worry about global warming, even when faced with evidence of changing microclimates?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Does a person worry about fertility and starting a family young, until they are actually trying and come across difficulties?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I know most of my patients never worried about breast cancer until they have a symptom or heard that a friend or colleague is recently diagnosed with breast cancer.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I want my children to grow up and take responsibility for themselves.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, I believe that everyone of us can take responsibility for our own health, but we need to be empowered on how to do this.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Humans are emotional creatures, but we have the capacity to think.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Learning how to regulate emotions and using our brains to think is an invaluable skill that can be taught from childhood.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I know some adults who still struggle with this.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I cannot underestimate the importance of having a scientific and logical framework in approach to all problems.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Fear, anger, worry, joy are all emotional responses that are normal but we must learn to regulate them.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Too often, I see my patients so paralysed by anxiety that it interferes with the treatment process.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some diseases are well-studied and the progression is clearly understood, for example, Hepatitis B leads to liver cancer and Hepatitis B vaccination is effective.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some others are multifactorial, such as most cancers and cardiovascular diseases.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: So, just because I smoke, it does not mean I will get lung cancer for sure.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, just because I do not smoke, it does not mean that I will never get lung cancer.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It is not so simple; there is no magic bullet or "免死金牌".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Obesity, strokes, heart attacks – we call these "lifestyle diseases" because every day, we make small decisions on food and activity level that will build up to or prevent these.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Do we recognise mental health issues or is it unseen until there is a sentinel event with self-harm?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Preventable trauma is another huge area we can improve on.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Awareness on child safety seats, road safety awareness by all users including pedestrians and cyclists, stricter regulations for driving licenses, giving way to emergency vehicles, workplace safety.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is so much to teach, so much to learn.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Education cannot be assigned to just the Ministry of Education (MOE), just as health should not be the domain of the MOH only.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am alarmed at how often I notice infants being spoon-fed while they are looking at an iPad.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have seen increasing numbers of young adult patients in their 20s with such problems and I am deeply concerned for the future generations.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Teaching the appropriate use of technology is not just for the young, but for the adults as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In relation to health, there are trends of miracle cures to fight cancer or guarantee weight loss.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have seen patients trying the black garlic diet, aloe vera, alkaline water, negative ion clothing.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I call this pseudoscience because there is a hint of truth in it.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is one experiment to show that the item has one property that has killed a few cancer cells in a petri dish.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: To me, this is like an observation that, "Hey, the ant can use a leaf to float on water!

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, if I use a big leaf, I can use it to sail across the ocean!" I cannot professionally extrapolate such studies to claim that it can cure cancer, which is what some salespeople do and vulnerable patients will try it and sometimes even forgo proven treatments.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Internet connectivity has brought people closer together but has also allowed misinformation to flourish.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: People rely on word-of-mouth recommendations, some use Google reviews and some people do not know that these can be bought or faked, or that there are malicious marketing agencies who deliberately downvote rival companies.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Whose role is it then to teach people how to use Google and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a tool?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It does not feel like it should be the Government's job.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Motivational speaker Jim Rohn said that, "You are the average of the five people you spend the most time with".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I use this to take stock of my personal and professional growth periodically.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Whenever I feel stagnant, time to review and change a bit, step out of the comfort zone, learn something new.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Do not settle in too comfortably and be trapped in an echo chamber.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: How do we then cultivate this mindset in people?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: This leads me to my next point: cross-collaboration.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I think the COVID-19 Multi-Ministry Task Force was a good platform for leadership to discuss and share timely information on a rapidly evolving situation and align policy direction.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, there were problems as it filtered down, because humans being humans, we have a wide range of responses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: We had people ranging from lawful good to chaotic evil, to use a Dungeons and Dragons reference.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some followed the exact letter of the law, some followed the spirit of what is intended.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Some profiteered off other's desperations and some wilfully, selfishly lived by their own rules and not respect the society they are living in.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The Government of Singapore is complex: organised into 16 Ministries, further divided into departments, divisions and more than 50 Statutory Boards.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Do people from different Ministries talk to one another, or is there a very strict protocol of how new ideas may be raised?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I ask because previously when working within the confines of a restructured hospital as an employee, I know that there are clear hierarchical processes.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: And even now, I only have experience talking to certain folks within MOH.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I know there are incredibly smart and devoted people in the Civil Service at all levels of seniority.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I know passionate and caring people who are active volunteers in various groups, charities and social enterprises.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is a flourishing ecosystem, but I wonder if perhaps there are too many small-to-medium groups.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Every one of us may be a domain expert, but we do not know what we do not know.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: From my participation in MHIC, I had the privilege of networking across different industries, to be acquainted with insurers, financial advisors, actuaries and to discuss healthcare problems from their point of view.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It was humbling to realise how little of healthcare financing I knew before, as a clinician.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am yet again bringing up the story of blind men examining the elephant and everyone only touching the part they can touch and arguing about what the elephant looks like.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Because it is true – we do not know what we do not know.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I now challenge you to think beyond your usual area and how you can apply your knowledge to better support healthcare, wherever you are in.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: You have heard the problems I brought up as a doctor, as a healthcare leader.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I respectfully share some of my ideas of how to align future policies, with the compass oriented towards healthcare.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that when people with similar goals and ideas discuss casually, the mind-mapping and synergy may create something way better.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Starting from young, the Early Childhood Development Agency and MOE can work closely with MOH to identify key basic health messages for young Singaporeans to learn.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: And the challenge is not in rote learning but how to get updates on information, because some scientific breakthroughs develop rapidly.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The food pyramid that I learnt in primary school is now outdated, replaced by the healthy plate model and current nutrition and fitness research is leaning towards low-carb diet with resistance training.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Teach children how to eat right and cultivate the habit of regular exercise to maintain a healthy weight.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: A lot has been done for mental health education and safe, appropriate use of social media in primary schools.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: These can also be adopted for adults who did not grow up in the Internet age, so that they are also taught about online etiquette and safety.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Introduce and strengthen the idea of the family doctor and the importance of good primary care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Teach how to navigate the healthcare system, how to get into subsidised care and the role of different types of insurance.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: MSF, in your mission to build strong families, could also collaborate with MOE and MOH to shape sex education, guide families on how to hold the tough conversations on morality, religious beliefs and identity.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Ask the coaching industry, especially those who specialise in sexuality counselling.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Teach older teenagers and tertiary students about the parenthood journey, its many joys but also hardships so that in time, young couples can make an informed decision about marriage and the pros and cons of having children or not, and when to have children; in their 20s, 30s or 40s?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Once we enter the workforce, we often neglect our own health to pursue a career.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In work with long hours or shifts, we develop unhealthy eating habits and irregular sleeping hours, and do not know how to make time to exercise.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: How many adults notice weight gain and lethargy over five or 10 years of working life?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporean men have their yearly individual physical proficiency test to clear but women might not have a fitness benchmark.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is a phenomenon of being "skinny fat", where the person has a healthy weight range but has low muscle and bone mass.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I think this is where all the different Ministries can contribute to health, by continuing education on diet and exercise, screening and vaccinations as well as empowering adults.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Ministries such as the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, MSF and Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) might be ideal to be the facilitators of cross-collaborations between the different Ministries.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Good ideas, content and projects can be supported by all, rather than every Ministry trying to come up with their own independent project.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If you Google "Singapore how to lose weight", see what comes up.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Articles on HealthXchange, HealthHub, Health Promotion Board (HPB) get buried amidst advertorials from aesthetics clinics, spas and gyms.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Repeat the same essential health messages in each of your various networks: eat right, exercise every day, protect your mental health, whichever division you are in, for social support, for youth or for sports.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I hope you continue to integrate sports into the community.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Are you aware that Singapore's cityscape is acknowledged as a parkour paradise internationally?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But practitioners frequently get chased away by residents who think they are vandalising and that the Police are called to chase them away.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I hope for stronger support for the parkour community in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I think that people still buy a lot of bubble tea even when graded "C" or "D"!

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I hope I did not miss anyone out.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: This has benefits such as a start towards food security and the health benefits of working with nature, learning to grow and eat our own organic foods will be lasting.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Information technology (IT) continues to be a huge challenge in so many aspects.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I said in a previous speech; electronic health records are sometimes nothing better than Microsoft Word documents or PDF documents scanned and stored online.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I do not know how this can be achieved, but can MCI, GovTech, Integrated Health Information Systems (iHIS) and other IT Statutory Boards please coordinate and get a good national system up?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I envision using Singpass and Healthhub, with trigger questions to remind the individual of major health checkpoints: height and weight; health screening; vaccinations; appointments.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Will MTI help MOH to attract Singaporeans to take up essential jobs in healthcare?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Look into the development of healthcare workers to recruit, train and retain experienced workers.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Human resource management will be essential, not to manage people as commodities, but to truly build a good working relationship for them, so that they feel appreciated and will stay for the long haul.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Complex medical conditions are managed by a multidisciplinary care team.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I apply a similar concept to our healthcare system problem.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Cross-collaborate; engage with healthcare providers; step outside of your comfort zones across the different Ministries and industries.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Appropriate remuneration for consultancy work may be something to consider and, in time, build up a network.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am very mindful of costs and ideally, if we can call upon volunteers, that would be great, but I also realise that runs the risk of the same few big-hearted people being called upon again and again.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Set up a think tank whom all the Ministries can have access to and call up on for brief consultations on global issues, not ad hoc requests to organisations.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I have explained why healthcare should be a whole-of-Government concern and not just MOH.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I emphasised the need for education at multiple levels of engagement and I asked for everyone to cross-collaborate.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: My old friend told me, "Don't pretend you want people to be healthy.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Ideally, I want to look after patients who become sick despite their best efforts, not those who have neglected themselves through the lack of knowledge, a lack of resources or lack of self-care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Let us work together to bring down the number of preventable illnesses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: It is our individual responsibility to keep as fit and healthy as we can.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As a society, to be kind and civic-minded.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: For those who hoarded medical supplies and tried to profiteer during COVID-19, shame on you!

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As a doctor, I look after all patients equally.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: But when intensive care unit beds are full, who deserves it?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare workers need the Government to help shape these policies.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Do not force us to have to have to triage and decide who to save.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Before I begin, I would like to declare that I am an orthodontist working at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound impact on the world, with healthcare workers playing a vital role in providing critical care to those who need it.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: As we begin to move beyond the pandemic, it is clear that we need to continue to prioritise and support healthcare.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This Motion acknowledges the importance of healthcare in our society and seeks to ensure that healthcare workers and patients alike receive the support and resources they need to thrive.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It recommends a whole-of-Government approach to build a healthier and more resilient society for all.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond the pandemic and towards the future, I would like to touch on three areas that require our continued attention and support: firstly, the manpower shortage of healthcare workers which is related to burnout and the mental well-being of healthcare workers; secondly, the provision of dental care to our migrant workers; and thirdly, supporting the special care and geriatric dentistry scene.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare workers have always faced intense stress, emotional situations and challenging working conditions, with long and unpredictable work hours, risk of injury and exposure to diseases.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: These factors can contribute to burnout and mental health issues, even before the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Although short-term measures such as counselling and mental health programmes are crucial, it is imperative to address the underlying root causes of burnout and mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This requires addressing systemic issues such as workload, work-life balance, support, training and the workplace culture.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: At the core of this is actually manpower shortage, which MOH is already trying to address.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, even globally, there is competition for a scarce healthcare workforce.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: In her Committee of Supply (COS) speech this year, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam mentioned that "The loss of both local and foreign nurses to our competitor countries is a key reason for the stress and high workload for our nurses.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: We need to replace the manpower lost to other countries, safeguard the welfare of nurses, and meet increasing needs." If we were to go one step further, we need to ensure that our healthcare workers are supported and have the resources they need to provide the best care possible, we need to build "fat", or buffer, into the system.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I have a few suggestions on how we can retain and attract healthcare manpower.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: MOH is supportive of fellow Nominated Member of Parliament (NMP) Dr Tan Yia Swam's suggestion of granting permanent resident status to foreign healthcare workers who are good performers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: For these good performers, can we go one step further and automatically grant their immediate family, namely spouse and children, permanent residency as well?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I know of several dental nurses at my workplace who have left due to this reason.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: After repeated applications, they have in the end given up, choosing instead to uproot their whole family to places such as Canada, New Zealand and Australia.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: If we grant permanent residency to their family, they will sink their roots in Singapore and the likelihood of losing them will reduce.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: When we lose good performers, especially senior ones, we do not just lose a worker, we lose their years of experience in our healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number two: ensuring remunerations are competitive locally and internationally.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I am aware that MOH monitors our pay competitiveness locally and internationally regularly.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Salary may not be the sole determining factor for healthcare workers, but it is still an important consideration for many individuals when choosing their career paths, especially with the tremendous demands of care work.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It can also incentivise foreign healthcare workers to continue working in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This is something Member Dr Tan Wu Meng has spoken about at length during the COS debates and it is something I cannot overstate the importance of.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare workers are also mothers, fathers, daughters and sons.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: They may have an elderly parent, or young children at home.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, there are already FWAs available for healthcare workers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, MOH and MOM can work together to come up with more creative permutations of flexible and family‐friendly human resources (HR) work practices suited for healthcare workers in different stages of their lives as well as the unique needs of each healthcare setting.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: For example, other than staggered shift times, we can consider having flexible shift lengths that split shifts into shorter scheduled times or offering healthcare workers even more paid leave.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number four: increasing the public's respect for healthcare workers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The public should understand that healthcare workers are not just transactional service providers who need to kowtow to the patient's demands.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: My fellow NMP Mr Raj Joshua Thomas will speak further on this topic.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number five: improving the home caregiving landscape by providing broader support and help.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: To relieve the healthcare sector, caregivers are the foundation of ageing-in-place.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, I have witnessed, from my relatives, how difficult the journey can be.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This is so that while they look after the needs of the elderly, we should also look at needs assessment for the caregiver itself so that they are not ignored, whether in self-care for their mental well-being or financial security when they themselves grow old.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Dental health is a very important health aspect that can be easily overlooked, but modern research has shown links between oral health, systemic health and quality of life.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: For example, gum disease can increase the risk of diabetes, infective endocarditis and other vascular diseases.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Dental pain due to neglect can also be debilitating.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot ignore the importance of oral health and its impact on overall health and quality of life.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, for the migrant workers, even if the dental treatment is deemed necessary, employers will have to bear the cost of dental treatment and dental treatment can be costly.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, the Primary Care Plan ensures accessible and affordable healthcare for eligible migrant workers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I would now like to speak about supporting the geriatric and special needs scene.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: As we work towards the goal of Healthier SG, we want to ensure oral health is addressed in successful ageing and inclusive healthcare.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Before I start, I would like to talk about the case of my colleague.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: A woman with a severe intellectual disability presented at the Geriatric and Special Care Dentistry Clinic for treatment.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Her challenging behaviour meant that treatment under local anaesthesia – that means when she is awake – was not viable.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, dental treatment under general anaesthesia, which is going to sleep, came with its own set of problems.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Risks outweighed the benefit, especially for a single tooth extraction.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, hospital policy requires legal representation for consent involving mentally incapacitated adults, and obtaining Court-appointed deputyship could take months and can be costly.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: To make matters worse, the woman had previously had a traumatic experience in the hospital environment.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Her family therefore chose chair-side management after weighing the options.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: After attempting to prepare her with three acclimatisation visits, the dentist attempted the extraction with physical restraints.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, due to profound difficulties faced, they just could not do it.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This experience highlighted the struggles faced not only by the patient's family in navigating the system, but also by the dentist and the medical team in treating individuals with complex needs.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number one: engaging elderly and special care needs patients and their communities.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The lack of oral health knowledge and health goals in these groups underscores the need for advocacy and mindset change.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Patients and caregivers often struggle to navigate the various services available and may not know who to approach for financial help and other supportive services.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: To address this, there may be a need for closer cross-collaboration between those involved in their care; professionals such as dentists, ward nurses and caregivers need to know basic oral health literacy as well as where to get reliable treatment information.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: We can consider looking at Nursing Practice Guidelines to ensure that oral care offered to residents is also up-to-date and practical.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number two: reserving capacity for those with complex needs.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Dentists are doing their best to help out, but there is a lack of guidance on standards of care.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
